When the posterior has a known closed form,
as in [the Beta-Bernoulli example](bayesian-inference.qmd#exm-beta-bernoulli),
we can compute its summaries exactly or sample from it directly.
In most real-world models, however,
the [marginal likelihood](bayesian-inference.qmd#def-marginal-likelihood) $\p(\vy)$ that normalizes the posterior
cannot be computed,
so neither can the posterior's summaries.
**Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC)** methods get around this problem:
instead of independent draws from the posterior,
they generate a *correlated* sequence of draws
whose distribution converges to the posterior
[@dobson4e, Chapter 13, p. 287].
